source: segmentation (Blender simulation render, background replaced by plain white)
units: pixels (image coords, x right, y down, origin top-left) and seconds; no metric scale estimated

objects.name: truck
objects.description: White/grey box truck with a white MAN-style cab facing right and a raised grey railing/stair platform on top of the box above the cab (aircraft catering truck). Only object in the video.
objects.clipping: frames 0-33 rear part cut off by left image edge; frames 44-58 front cut off by right image edge; frame 58 only a tiny remnant (rear corner, 3865 px); frame 59 empty
objects.reference_point_note: Blender vehicle root is not visible. Best proxies: axles_mid (midpoint of front and rear wheel hubs, at axle height) or a single wheel hub. Ground-contact proxies: *_tyre_bottom_y under each hub. Mask centroid/bbox are only meaningful in fully_in_view frames 34-43.

parts.front_hub: centre of the front (steer) wheel hub, below the cab
parts.rear_hub: centre of the rear wheel hub, under the box
parts.front_bumper_right: right-most point of the front bumper (yellow marker light corner), the truck's leading point in the image
parts.box_rear_top / box_rear_bottom: top and bottom of the rear vertical edge of the cargo box (near side)
parts.stairs_top: top rail of the platform/railing structure above the cab, near its left post

static_objects: none - the background was replaced by uniform white; no ground, markings, shadows or other objects are visible

measurements_at_frame_34_px.note: frame 34 is the first frame with the whole truck in view (smallest full view); frame 43 the last (largest)

events.event: truck essentially at rest / starting to move: front hub moves 0.56 px from frame 0 to 1, 1.7 px from 1 to 2, then the per-frame step grows steadily (speeding up throughout the clip, no braking, no direction change)
rear wheel hub enters the image at the left edge
rear of the box clears the left image edge: whole truck in view (frames 34-43)
front bumper reaches the right image edge; truck starts leaving the view
front wheel hub leaves the image at the right edge
rear wheel hub leaves the image at the right edge
last frame with any of the truck visible (tiny rear-corner remnant)

camera.motion: assumed static (simulation convention: camera fixed within a clip). Cannot be verified from the image because the background is uniform white; the truck's vanishing point stays constant (see below), consistent with a fixed camera and a straight-driving truck.
camera.vp_note: intersection of the box top edge line and the hub-to-hub line, frames 16-56: x between -2930 and -3170, y 534-548 (median about -3030, 538). Stable => the truck does not yaw; it drives straight along its own axis (front hub trajectory also points at this VP). The VP lies at y ~ 538 ~ image centre row 540, so the horizon of the (invisible) ground plane is at y ~ 538 and the camera is close to level (no pitch, no visible roll).
camera.motion_direction_in_image: right and slightly down (toward the camera): front hub goes from (52, 801) at frame 0 to (1484, 918) at frame 43; the truck approaches the camera, so its apparent size grows
camera.apparent_size_change: wheelbase hub-to-hub 331 px (f0, rear hub extrapolated) -> 374 (f20) -> 498 (f34) -> 668 (f43) -> 914 (f50) -> 1273 (f57, extrapolated); box rear edge height 225 (f0, extrapolated) -> 248 (f20) -> 292 (f34) -> 328 (f43) -> 375 (f50) -> 447 (f57); front wheel radius 54.7 (f0) -> 58.9 (f20) -> 69 (f34) -> 79.5 (f43) -> 84.8 (f46). Per-frame values in tracks/truck.csv. Length-like measures grow faster than heights because the truck is also seen less foreshortened as it comes nearer and moves right.
